## Scheduled jobs

[node-cron](https://github.com/node-cron/node-cron). `jobs/heartbeat.job.js` is a worked example (logs once a minute) — add a real job by creating a file the same shape (`cronExpression` + `run()`) and listing it in `jobs/index.js`. Jobs start once everything else in `loaders/index.js` has finished connecting, and stop cleanly on shutdown.

**Running more than one instance of this API?** node-cron runs in-process — N horizontally-scaled instances means the same job fires N times on the same schedule (duplicate emails, double-run cleanups, ...). This is a real, easy-to-miss gotcha, not a hypothetical: if that's a risk here, either pass `{ distributed: true }` to `schedule()` in `jobs/index.js` and wire up a coordinator (node-cron ships the `distributed` option and a pluggable `RunCoordinator` interface for exactly this — see https://nodecron.com/distributed-coordination), or use the `queue-bullmq` module's repeatable jobs instead, which coordinate through Redis by design and never double-fire across instances.

Not using scheduled jobs yet? This module is safe to leave installed and unused, or delete `jobs/` and the `node-cron` dependency entirely.
